results.question: Summarise where the garden shed project stands.
results.expect: A summary covering budget, cedar decision, Tomás framing in October, no permit needed, and open tasks.
cites: Meeting with Tomás about the shed
sources: Meeting with Tomás about the shed
results.answer:
Garden shed status (as of the latest notes)

Planning & permits – The shed (7.2 m², 2.3 m tall) meets the council’s criteria for no‑permit construction and sits 1.5 m from the fence. No permit required. [4]
Budget – €3,200 ceiling set. €2,420 spent (foundation blocks €340, cedar cladding €1,150, roofing felt & battens €410, door/window €520). Remaining €780 covers fixings, paint and surprises. [2]
Materials – Western red cedar chosen over pine, costing about €300 more but no preservative needed. Decision made 20 Sep. [5]
Progress
Ground leveled and foundation blocks laid (completed 2 Oct). [3]
Cedar ordered and received. [3]
Tomás will frame walls and roof on the weekends of 11 Oct and the following weekend (labour €600). [6]
Upcoming tasks
Install roofing felt after framing.
Hang door and window.
Paint trim.
Decide on adding a gutter and water butt.
Timeline – Target finish before the November rains; tasks still pending but the core structure is set to be completed in October. [1]

results.question: What hydration should I use for my sourdough?
results.expect: Says the notes disagree: 75% at home, 68% at altitude; cites both sides.
results.answer:
Use 75 % hydration for most of your sourdough loaves—this yields the best open crumb and is confirmed by your own notes [1][2].
If you’re baking at high altitude (e.g., 1 800 m), drop the hydration to 68 % because 75 % tends to spread flat there [3].

results.question: How quickly did printing spread across Europe after Gutenberg?
results.expect: Mainz scattering in 1462, Italy 1465, Paris 1470, Caxton 1476, over 250 cities by 1500; facts from several chunks of the long clip.
cites: How the printing press changed Europe
sources: How the printing press changed Europe
results.answer: Printing spread very rapidly after Gutenberg’s breakthrough. After the sack of Mainz in 1462, printers dispersed across Europe, and by the mid‑1460s presses had appeared in Italy (1465), Paris (1470) and Spain (1472). By 1500 there were presses in more than 250 European cities, with an estimated 15–20 million incunabula printed in that period.  [1]

results.question: ¿Qué ingredientes necesito para las arepas?

results.answer:
Los ingredientes que necesitas para las arepas son:

2 tazas de harina de maíz precocida (P.A.N.)
2 tazas y media de agua tibia
1 cucharadita de sal
Un poco de mantequilla
Queso blanco para rellenar (si lo deseas)
